full_judgment:
5. The learned counsel for the pre-emptee petitioner submits that the High Court Division fell in error in not considering that the deed dated 27.7.87, against which pre-emption is sought, is not in fact a transfer deed as in the same value of the case land was shown at merely Tk. 98/- and further the possession of the land covered under the above deed was also not delivered and so the above deed may be termed as a deed for protection of possession of the pre-emptee petitioner against which a pre-emption case is not maintainbale; the appellate Court correctly found that the pre-emptee is not wholly a stranger in view of the fact that her husband Ranju Miah was one of the co-sharers in the R.S. Khatian No. 2480 and further as the B.S. Record was not correctly prepared and for that the recorded tenant executed and registered the above deed dated 27.7.87 for removal of that mistake and the said deed as is in fact not a sale deed; the High Court Division having had failed to take notice that the pre-emptee petitioner was not a stranger to the case jote and that she has been possessing the case land and residing in the homestead situated therein for long time and if the pre-emption case is allowed the paternal homestead of the petitioner will go into the hand of the pre-emptor. 

 6. As it appears the High Court Division made the Rule absolute holding that the pre-emptor purchased a portion of the case jote by Ext. 5(Ka) and his name was recorded in the B.S. record, Ext.3, in Khatian No. 54 and the rent receipts Ext.4 series, also show that he, after purchasing the said land, mutated his name and paid rents regularly and he, as co-sharer, is in possession in the case land and the B.S. Khatian which has been published finally does not contain the name of the pre-emptee and the pre-emptee has also not challenged that preparation of B.S. Khatian in the name of the pre-emptor and so prima facie the pre-emptor appears to be a co-sharer and further the title of the pre-emptor in the case land can be challenged by the pre-emptee only in a properly constituted title suit.
